findings.title: Used-up federated recovery codes are removed through the local store API, which does nothing for them.
findings.body: `getCredential` can now return a credential from user storage. If all of its codes are used, the code still calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only deletes from the local database. The federated model may have no id at all: the test provider builds it with `createFromValues` and no id. The user-storage copy is never removed, so the user keeps a credential with no codes left and is not sent to the setup required action that normally follows. Fix: when the credential is federated, remove it through the user storage path, for example `disableCredentialType` or `updateCredential`.

findings.title: Federated recovery codes are never used up and any code is accepted.
findings.body: `isValid` returns true if the input matches any stored code. It never removes the matched code. The local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` consumes each code on use, but nothing does that for a federated credential. `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` then rebuilds the model from all stored codes, so the login page always asks for the first code while any of the 12 is accepted, and a code can be used again forever. This is the reference provider for the new path, so the test cannot catch the broken one-time-use rule. Fix: check only the requested next code, then remove it and persist the remaining list (for example through `updateCredential`), or have the authenticator update the federated credential after a successful login.

held.title: getCredentials dereferences getMyUser without the null check the other methods have.
held.body: `getMyUser(user)` returns null when the username is not in the map. `isConfiguredFor` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` guard against that, but `getCredentials` reads `myUser.recoveryCodes` straight away and throws a NullPointerException. Return `Stream.empty()` when `myUser` is null.
